days.headline: Rabies bill debated; vote later
days.summary: The second reading debate was adjourned without a vote. The House next sits on 3 November.

items.title: Rabies and dog registration bill
items.what: Second reading debated and adjourned to a later date. No vote was taken.

figs.l: maximum fine, e.g. abandoning a dog

items.next: Debate resumes on a date still to be set

items.title: Anti-terrorism bill: another court petition
items.what: The Speaker announced a further petition against the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill.

items.title: Public Finance committee report presented
items.what: Presented by Nimal Palihena, Member of the Committee, for its Chair.
points: Annual reports for 2025: Regional Development Bank; Jaya Container Terminals Limited.
Petitions: one from Nilanthi Kottahachchi and two from R.M. Samantha Ranasinghe, referred to the Committee on Public Petitions.

items.title: Poverty programme figures
items.what: The Prajashakthi national poverty eradication programme, from a written answer published on 23 October.
points: Minister of Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment Upali Pannilage, answering Ajith Gihan.
Projects started: 15,316 livelihood, 273 education and 136 health.

items.title: Raised: Asian Games, teachers, pasture lands
items.what: Urgent questions, two ministerial replies and an adjournment motion on tourism.
points: K. Kader Masthan: exclusion of Fathima Shafiya from the 20th Asian Games in Japan.
Shanakiyan Rasamanickam: teacher recruitment, and Development Officers not absorbed into the Teachers' Service.
Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation K.D. Lal Kantha: pasture lands in Madavanai, replying to a question of 23 September.
Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government A.H.M.H. Abayarathna: local authorities in the Northern and Eastern Provinces, replying to a question of 25 September.
Nishantha Perera: adjournment motion on Benthara, Karandeniya and Elpitiya as new tourism zones.

days.headline: Two drug-law bills passed
days.summary: Both drug-law amendments passed with changes. Nine annual reports approved, four from 2015 to 2018.

items.title: Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Bills
items.what: Bill 79 covers how seized drugs are handled and destroyed. Bill 80 covers methamphetamine, manufacturing and bail.

items.title: Anti-terrorism bill: more court petitions
items.what: Further petitions against the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill.

items.title: Nine annual reports approved
points: Janatha Estates Development Board: 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018
National Institute of Labour Studies: 2022
National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health: 2022
Ranaviru Seva Authority: 2023
Kotelawala Defence University: 2022, 2023

items.title: Committee report and three annual reports tabled
items.what: The Governance, Justice and Civil Protection oversight committee reported.
points: 2024 annual reports: Official Languages Commission; Ceylon German Technical Training Institute; Institute of Human Resource Advancement, University of Colombo.

items.title: Figures given to the House
points: Rabies: Minister of Health and Mass Media Nalinda Jayatissa.
Fences: Minister of Environment Dammika Patabendi.
Pepper: Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Livestock Namal Karunaratne.

items.title: Answers on reserves and El Niño
items.what: Replies to questions held over from August and September.
points: Official reserves: Anil Jayantha, Minister of Labour and Deputy Minister of Finance, replying to Ravi Karunanayake (asked 18 August).
El Niño and recovery after Cyclone Ditwah: Deputy Minister of Defence Aruna Jayasekera, replying to Sajith Premadasa.

items.title: Raised: 2026 Budget progress, Middle East conflict
items.what: Urgent questions, and an adjournment motion on a diplomatic reception.
points: Sajith Premadasa: progress of the 2026 Budget proposals.
Ravi Karunanayake: economic impact of the conflict involving the US, Israel and Iran.
Dilith Jayaweera: motion on the reception for Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister.

days.headline: Borrowing resolution and extra spending approved
days.summary: Amounts are not in the same-day record. They follow with the Hansard.

items.title: Debt resolution, Public Debt Management Act
items.what: Amount and terms not yet published.

src.t: Public Debt Management Act, No. 33 of 2024

items.title: Supplementary Estimate No. 06 of 2026
items.what: Extra spending for the Department of Development Finance (Head 243).

items.title: Trusts (Amendment) Bill
items.what: Amends the Trusts Ordinance (Chapter 87).

items.title: Court petitions on three bills
items.what: Sri Lanka Cricket, anti-terrorism and Immigration bills.

items.title: Public finance and debt reports
items.what: Committee on Public Finance report and the debt office's 2025 performance report.
points: Also: the Environment, Agriculture and Resource Sustainability oversight committee report.
Follow-ups to Committee on Public Accounts findings: Ministry of Digital Economy, Ministry of Technology, Western Provincial Council.

items.title: Ten annual reports approved
points: Sri Lanka Export Development Board: 2021, 2022, 2023
National Gem and Jewellery Authority: 2022, 2023
Gem and Jewellery Research and Training Institute: 2023
National Salt Ltd: 2021/22, 2022/23
BCC Lanka Ltd: 2021/22, 2022/23

items.title: Prison numbers
points: Minister of Justice and National Integration Harshana Nanayakkara.
Largest age group: 30 to 40, with 3,423 prisoners.

items.title: Raised: liquor licences, remembrance day, Sathurukondan inquiry
items.what: Urgent questions and ministerial statements.
points: Shanakiyan Rasamanickam: illegal liquor and new liquor licences.
Ramanathan Archchuna: Thileepan remembrance day.
Minister of Public Security Ananda Wijepala: the Sathurukondan killings inquiry, and ethnic harmony and national security.

days.headline: Security bills presented; container inquiry extended
days.summary: A customs duty order and seven education orders reached the House, one of them 887 days after it was gazetted.

items.title: Organised Crimes and Foreign Terrorist Fighters bills
items.what: Give effect to a UN convention and UN Security Council Resolution 2178.

items.title: Customs import duty order, Gazette 2502/21
items.next: Rates to be added from the Gazette

items.title: Seven higher-education orders
items.what: New private degrees and two name changes.
points: Degrees: SLIIT, Sri Lanka Technology Campus, KIU Campus, The American College of Higher Education, Sri Lanka Institute of Textile and Apparel.
Renamed: SLT Campus; Esoft Metro Campus, now Esoft Uni.

items.title: Court petitions: Cricket and anti-terrorism bills
Supplementary Estimate No. 06 presented
items.what: Approved the next day.

items.title: Inquiry into uninspected containers extended
items.what: Containers released from Colombo Port without the mandatory physical inspection.
points: The select committee was set up by a resolution of 19 November 2025.

items.title: Anti-corruption oversight committee
items.what: Oversees Parliament's part in the National Anti-Corruption Action Plan 2025 to 2029.

items.title: Auditor-General reports and papers
points: Annual reports include Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation and its life and general companies (2025), ITN, the National Transport Commission and the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation (2024).
Committee on Public Accounts follow-ups: Department for Registration of Persons; local authorities in the Central and Western provinces.

items.title: Statements: power outage, tusker Kavantissa
items.what: The island-wide outage of 17 October, and the death of a tusker.
points: Minister of Energy Anura Karunathilaka, replying to Ravi Karunanayake.
Minister of Environment Dammika Patabendi, replying to Sajith Premadasa.
Adjournment motion on the country's situation: Gayantha Karunathilleka.
The opposition asked for a debate on delays in filling Supreme Court and Court of Appeal vacancies.

items.title: Anti-Corruption (Amendment) certified
items.what: Signed by the Speaker. Printed as Act No. 25 of 2026.

days.headline: Court rulings on the drug-law bills read out

items.title: Supreme Court determinations: drug-law bills
items.what: Bill 79 needs two amendments to pass by simple majority; Bill 80 can pass as it stands.

items.title: Annual reports tabled and referred
items.what: Includes the Sri Lanka Fisheries Corporation annual report for 2020.
points: Fisheries Corporation report referred to the oversight committee on environment, agriculture and natural resources.
Public petitions referred to the Committee on Public Petitions.

items.title: Employment of persons with disabilities
points: Answer given by the Deputy Minister, Wasantha Piyathissa.
Subsidy covers 50% of salary.

items.title: Regional Development Bank branches and staff
points: Answer given by the Deputy Minister, Nishantha Jayaweera.
Eight provincial offices to merge into four regional offices.

items.title: Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill
items.what: Second and third readings, without a division.

items.title: Customs duty order, Gazette 2501/88
items.what: Section 10A order under the Customs Ordinance.

items.title: Auditor-General reports, including an EV audit
items.what: Includes a special audit report on electric vehicle use.

items.title: Tourism spending

figs.l: World Bank funding for northern tourism

points: Deputy Minister of Tourism Ruwan Ranasinghe, replying to Rajeevan Jeyachandramoorthy.

items.title: 2027 Appropriation Bill
items.what: Government spending and borrowing for 2027.

items.title: Immigration Bill
items.what: Would replace the 1948 immigration law and the 1971 passport law.

items.title: Export Agriculture (Amendment) certified
items.what: Act No. 24 of 2026, certified 6 October.

items.title: Diesel subsidy
points: Minister of Energy Anura Karunathilaka, during questions.
